A distance time graph is the graph with x-axis represented by Time and Y-axis by Distance. This graph is used to calculate the average speed (velocity) of a man or object moving from one point to another. It can also be used to get the time spent to get to a point from a reference point. OP and OQ are called the arms of the angle. Classification of angles Angles are classified as follows; a. Acute : the angle that is less than 90o b. Right angle: the angle that equals to 90o c. Obtuse: the angle that is greater than 90o d. Straight line angle: the angle that is half of a turn’ it is equal to 180o e. Reflex : the angle that is greater than 180o but less than 360o P ACUTE RIGHT ANGLE O Q

Total number of balls = 20 Number of white balls = 8 Probability of selecting a Content In everyday activities, we encounter events or experiments whose results we cannot predict in advance. Such experiments are called random experiments. - Probability is a measure of the likelihood of a required outcome happening. - An outcome is the result of an experiment in probability. An event, such as throwing a die, can have different outcomes. For instance, since it has six faces, the probability of throwing a 3 must be one out of six (1 6), since there are six different numbers (six possible outcomes). Therefore, probability is defined in form of a ratio as: 𝑁𝑢𝑚𝑏𝑒𝑟 𝑜𝑓 𝑠𝑢𝑐𝑐𝑒𝑠𝑠𝑓𝑢𝑙/𝑟𝑒𝑞𝑢𝑖𝑟𝑒𝑑 𝑜𝑢𝑡𝑐𝑜𝑚𝑒𝑠 𝑇𝑜𝑡𝑎𝑙 𝑛𝑢𝑚𝑏𝑒𝑟 𝑜𝑓 𝑝𝑜𝑠𝑠𝑖𝑏𝑙𝑒 𝑜𝑢𝑡𝑐𝑜𝑚𝑒𝑠 Probability can be written as a fraction, decimal or percentage. Note: 1. Probability is always measured as a value between 0 and 1. 2. Probability of an impossible event = 0. 3. Probability an event occurring + probability of the event not occurring = 1. Examples: 1. Out of 100 mangoes, five are bad. What is the probability that a mango chosen at random is good? Solution:
